native_result.query: What is the average length of original papers in Experimental Economics and that in Psychology?
native_result.HypoA: Studies in Experimental Economics tend to have longer original papers compared to Psychology. The average length of original papers in Experimental Economics is 28 pages, whereas in Psychology, the average is 11 pages.
native_result.HypoB: In this replication-project sample, the recorded original papers in Experimental Economics are substantially longer than those in Psychology: the 18 original papers from the Experimental Economics replication project (project='ee') average 28.0 pages (median 27.5, SD 7.4, 95% bootstrap CI 24.8-31.4), whereas the 95 original papers from the Reproducibility Project: Psychology (project='rpp', the headline definition of Psychology) average 11.2 pages (median 9.0, SD 6.3, 95% bootstrap CI 10.0-12.5) - a difference of 16.8 pages (about 2.5x; Welch p = 7.3e-09, Mann-Whitney p = 5.2e-10, Cohen's d = 2.57, 95% CI 1.97-3.18). The same figures hold under the broader pooled definition of Psychology (ml1+ml3+rpp, 117 papers, 11.16 pages, gap 16.8 pages), under id-level de-duplication, and after excluding or winsorising short brief reports (gap 13.4-17.9 pages). This is a difference in recorded page counts within this sample of replication targets, not evidence that economics papers are generally longer than psychology papers: the economics side is 18 papers from only two journals (American Economic Review 16, Quarterly Journal of Economics 2) whose page conventions are a format artefact, while the psychology side reflects RPP sampling short-format outlets (PS 39, JPSP 29, JEPLMC 27; 8 of 95 papers are 3 pages or shorter).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded only the study-level meta-regression CSV (927 rows x 57 cols). Built original-paper identity from a normalised key (case/whitespace-folded title + journal + volume + issue, missing volume/issue as its own level) and verified it reproduces the 135-group partition of title-only, with length/discipline/project constant inside every group. Collapsed the 927 original-by-replication-lab rows to 135 unique original papers (headline) and 141 original-study ids (robustness). Computed n, mean, median, SD, IQR, quartiles, min, max, skew per group, plus bootstrap 95 percent CIs by resampling papers with replacement (B=10000, numpy default_rng seed 20261022, percentile method; difference CI seed 20261023) with degeneracy and discreteness diagnostics. Tested ee vs rpp and ee vs pooled psychology with Welch t, Mann-Whitney U, Cohen's d with Hedges g and CI, Hodges-Lehmann shift and the common-language probability. Produced the full per-project table (ee/ml1/ml3/rpp) plus pooled psychology, a separately labelled wrong-but-diagnostic block of row-level naive means with the ml1 65.1 percent weight argument, and a sensitivity grid (exclude length<=3, winsorise at pooled p5/p95, id-level de-dup, drop==FALSE). Verified the drop column empirically (0 ee and 0 ml3 rows, 3 ml1 and 7 rpp papers touched, economics delta exactly 0.0000) and confirmed file 2 has no length field so no join was performed. Cross-checked the headline means by hand (ee 504/18 = 28.0000; rpp 1067/95 = 11.2316).
